name: The Gates Scholarship
value: Last-dollar full cost of attendance after other aid and Student Aid Index or college methodology, for up to five years toward a bachelor’s degree.
deadline: Phase I: July 15-September 15, 2026. Semifinalists/Phase II open December 1, 2026; Phase II due January 15, 2027. Finalists March 1, 2027; interviews March 1-31, 2027; Scholars April 20, 2027; funds fall 2027. Time zones are not stated.
apply: Create a myTGS profile and submit the online Phase I application; invited semifinalists complete Phase II, and finalists interview in person or virtually if no nearby interviewer. Public FAQ does not enumerate the complete phase-specific materials.
eligibility: High school seniors who are Pell-eligible, US citizens or permanent residents, with a minimum cumulative weighted GPA of 3.3 on a 4.0 scale, planning to enroll full time in a four-year degree at a US accredited not-for-profit college or university.
notes: Class of 2027 Phase I deadline has passed. Top-10% standing is an ideal-candidate factor, not a mandatory cutoff. No GED route or initial associate-degree transfer route; any major is allowed at a qualifying U.S./territory not-for-profit bachelor’s institution. Annual FAFSA, renewal form/current transcripts, each-term enrollment verification and satisfactory academic progress are required; approved deferral up to one year carries no funding.

name: Dell Scholars Program
value: $20,000 flexible scholarship plus a laptop, book credits and emergency funds; can also be used for graduate school, loan repayment, study abroad and internship stipends
deadline: Opens October 1, 2026; application January 12, 2027; finalists January 21, 2027; finalist materials March 31, 2027; college choice and award letter May 6, 2027; Scholars May 20, 2027. No time zone stated.
apply: Apply online; finalists submit a current high school transcript, FAFSA Submission Summary and other requested information. Finalists also provide college choice and award letter by the stated stage deadline; the public 2027 page does not enumerate all additional materials.
eligibility: High school seniors graduating from a Texas high school who participated in an approved college readiness program in grades 11 and 12, are Pell Grant eligible, have at least a 2.4 GPA, and plan to enroll at an accredited four-year public college or university in Texas.
notes: 2027 eligibility specifically requires a Texas high school, participation in a currently approved readiness program in grades 11 and 12, and an accredited Texas public four-year college. The general historical nationwide program description is not the 2027 eligibility list. The $20,000 is a flexible total award; detailed continuing access and disbursement conditions are not public. Career resources say unused funds may remain available within ten years, subject to eligibility.

name: Chick-fil-A Community Scholars
value: Up to $25,000 (one-time award, may be disbursed over 1 to 6 years); 13 awards per year, plus a year-long leadership development and mentorship program
deadline: 2027 cycle: August 21-November 3, 2026, at 3:00 p.m. Central Time. At least one online recommendation is due within three business days after November 3, 2026; applicants notified spring 2027.
apply: Apply through Scholarship America with complete current transcript, first two pages of parents’ IRS1040/T1 (or own if not dependent), and at least one online recommendation (up to three may be listed). Upload all required documents electronically and redact sensitive account/SSN data.
eligibility: Current high school seniors, undergraduates or graduate students with at least 3.0 cumulative GPA, who will be 18 by July 15, 2027 and reside in the U.S., Puerto Rico or Canada at application and award. Plan full-time undergraduate/graduate study in 2027-28 at an accredited two/four-year, vocational/technical or CEGEP institution. Service, activities or leadership in the preceding 12 months and willingness to join the one-year Scholars program are required. DACA and international students are expressly eligible.
notes: Up to 13 awards of up to $25000, one-time only; may be disbursed over one to six years, then unused funds forfeited. Past recipients cannot reapply. Education expenses paid to school, not student loans or refunds. Finalists must demonstrate financial need. Chick-fil-A employees and dependents/spouses of employees or Operators are ineligible.

name: Toyota Scholarship Program (Making Life Easier Scholars)
value: Tentative 2027 terms: $7500 annually, renewable for three further continuous years (up to $30000 total), subject to full-time satisfactory performance and program continuation.
deadline: Applications are closed. The administrator labels upcoming-cycle information tentative; no 2027 application closing date is published. Tentative notification is by the end of February 2027.
apply: Tentative 2027 process: online essays and financial information, signed partner-verification form, complete transcript (not grade report), and 2025 IRS1040 or an explanation if not filed. Confirm final requirements when applications open.
eligibility: Tentative 2027 terms: member or alumni within three years of a specifically listed nonprofit/school partner; senior, graduate or current undergraduate with diploma/GED by September 2027, 2.0 cumulative GPA, good disciplinary/academic standing, demonstrated need, and full-time qualifying U.S. undergraduate study throughout 2027-28. Toyota employee/vendor/business-partner and specified family/household exclusions apply.
notes: The actual 2027 partner list is specific to organizations/schools, not all students in a listed city. Chandler Education Foundation is limited to Chandler High School students. Tentative awards are undergraduate-only for 2027 recipients; prior cohorts may have graduate renewal. Renewal depends on full-time satisfactory academic performance and Toyota continuation. Upcoming terms are explicitly tentative.

name: McDonald's HACER National Scholarship
value: Sponsor states a $1 million total pool for up to 100 students. Individual award amounts, duration and renewal are not stated on the current public pages.

eligibility: High school seniors under 21 with a minimum 2.8 GPA who are legal US residents, US citizens or DREAMER/DACA recipients, eligible to attend a two- or four-year college, university or vocational/technical school full time in the academic year after selection.
notes: Current page says applications are closed. Selection includes need, academics, service, personal statement and interview; no separate essay is required. Current eligibility page states no heritage requirement, so none is imposed here. Individual award terms and 2027 dates need confirmation.

name: Jimmy Rane Foundation Scholarship
value: $500 to $6,000 per year, renewable annually for up to four academic years (eight semesters)
deadline: Application opens December 1, 2026 and closes February 5, 2027; recommendation letters due February 10, 2027. Awardees notified by phone in mid-April.
apply: Apply through the ISTS portal with all requested supplemental materials by February 5, 2027; recommendation materials have a February 10, 2027 exception. The public FAQ discusses test scores and family financial information but does not enumerate every upload.
eligibility: Spring/summer 2027 high school seniors with 3.0 GPA, GED recipients by June 30, 2027, or full-time college freshmen/sophomores with 2.75 GPA; applicants must be no older than 20 on August 1, 2027. U.S. citizens or permanent residents residing at a permanent home address in AL, AR, DE, FL, GA, IL, IN, IA, KS, KY, LA, MD, MS, MO, NE, NJ, NY, NC, OH, OK, PA, SC, TN, TX, VA, WV or DC. The FAQ additionally says permanent residents must be in the process of becoming U.S. citizens.
notes: Need influences selection and award size; $500-$6000 yearly for up to four academic years/eight semesters, contingent on renewal requirements that are not fully public. Other aid can reduce the amount; a full-expense scholarship must be reported. No intercollegiate student-athlete participation in the prior or coming semester/year, or exclusively online degree. Great Southern Wood family/household exclusions apply. Any major leading to a bachelor’s, with a technical-school non-degree exception, may qualify.

name: Sachs Foundation Undergraduate Scholarship
value: $10,000 to $12,500 per year, renewable for up to four years ($40,000 to $50,000 total)
deadline: The page gives an undated annual January 1-March 15 application window, March 31 recommendation deadline, late-April finalist notice and required June program. No explicit 2027 dates or time zone confirmed.
apply: Apply online with transcript, two non-relative recommendations, two 500-word personal statements, FAFSA Student Aid Report and household tax return information; optional portfolio.
eligibility: Black Colorado high school seniors resident full-time in Colorado for at least three years; military-order residence may be considered individually. Attend an accredited institution full-time for undergraduate study.
notes: Typical $10000-$12500 annual award, disbursed evenly each term, for up to four years ($40000-$50000 total). Detailed renewal standards are not published. Two 500-word statements, two non-relative recommendations, transcript, FAFSA SAR (the page retains that older term) and latest household tax information are required; an extra portfolio is optional. Finalists must attend a program in Colorado Springs before final approval. Confirm next-cycle aid-report requirements when the form opens.

name: Horatio Alger Scholarships for High School Seniors (Denny Sanford, Washington Foundation and Bergeron awards)
value: Denny Sanford awards: Arizona State 25 x $10,000; Augustana 6 x $25,000; Black Hills State 12 x $12,500; Dakota State 15 x $10,000; Long Island University 6 x $40,000. Dennis & Phyllis Washington Foundation (Montana): 50 x $10,000 plus $5,000 institutional match. Bergeron Everglades Environmental Steward (Florida): 4 x $20,000.
deadline: Undated senior application window: December 1-February 15, noon Eastern Time. The dated toolkit still lists December 1, 2025-February 15, 2026 and February 20, 2026 counselor/support forms; no confirmed 2027 dates.
apply: One online application generally covers eligible listed programs, except designated specialized programs. Submit adversity/American Dream responses, counselor certification, support verification by a non-relative adult over 21, transcript with fall grades and appropriate income verification. Confirm program-specific form deadlines.
eligibility: U.S. citizens with family adjusted gross income at most $100000, perseverance through adversity and commitment to a bachelor’s. Denny Sanford senior awards require full-time senior status, 2.5 GPA and immediate enrollment at the named university. Washington requires a Montana senior, 2.0 GPA and listed Montana institutions. Bergeron allows Florida seniors or college students, 2.0 GPA and a Florida environmental-sciences/studies degree.
notes: Grouped programs have distinct rules and funding schedules; duration and renewal conditions are not fully public. Washington’s extra $5000 institutional match excludes listed community and tribal colleges. Bergeron is not limited to seniors. The $25000 National Scholarship is a separate junior program. Current pages list award counts and totals without dated 2027 confirmation.

name: Royal Neighbors of America Member Scholarships
value: Award amounts not stated on the official scholarship page
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted; the 2026 application ran January 5 to March 2, 2026 (midnight Central Time).
apply: Use your Royal Neighbors certificate number to create an application account. Supply a high school transcript showing at least 2.5 GPA, or if graduation was more than ten years ago, strong work history and a professional reference. The 2026 announcement also describes leadership and service personal essays; the next-cycle form is unavailable.
eligibility: Royal Neighbors Beneficial Members over 16 pursuing an accredited trade/vocational, associate, bachelor’s, master’s or doctoral degree. Qualifying membership includes eligible life-insurance insureds (excluding Extended Term Insurance), annuity owners or trust annuitants, and settlement-contract owners. The transcript route requires 2.5 GPA; graduates over ten years ago may substitute work history and a reference.
notes: Maximum four years of support, with a new application each year and discretionary selection. Award amount is not stated. Program is not guaranteed and not available in all states. The published related-party exclusion sentence is ambiguous about member children/grandchildren; obtain clarification before relying on that portion.

name: Work Ethic Scholarship Program
value: Individual amounts vary. The first reported round awarded $500-$34000, averaging about $9100; this is a reported cohort range, not a guaranteed award schedule. Duration and renewal terms could not be confirmed.
deadline: Current page accepts applications through October 31 and lists April 30, June 30, August 30 and October 31 rounds, with June/August/October/December decisions. These dates have no explicit year in the page text; no confirmed 2027 cycle deadline.
apply: Apply through the linked ISTS portal. Sign the S.W.E.A.T. Pledge, answer four short questions, record an introduction video, supply two teacher/employer/supervisor reference contacts, latest transcript and an official tuition bill or cost statement.
eligibility: US citizens who are high school seniors or graduates enrolling in an approved skilled-trades program of two years or less at an accredited school.
notes: Approved skilled-trade programs last at most two years; four-year programs are excluded. Read the actual approved-program list and confirm school/program acceptance. The linked July 2026 guideline PDF remained inaccessible through direct and browser alternatives, leaving detailed award and processing terms unresolved.

name: TheDream.US National Scholarship
value: Published 2026-27 terms: tuition/fees up to $16500 for an associate degree or $33000 total for a bachelor’s, plus a stipend of up to $6000 stated on the main page. Next-cycle amounts are not confirmed.
deadline: The next round opens November 1, 2026. No confirmed 2027 closing date or acceptance deadline; the linked 2026-27 guide closes February 28, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time.
apply: Apply online through ISTS and separately apply to a qualifying partner college. The linked prior-cycle guide requires relevant high school/GED and post-high-school college transcripts, financial/dependency information, responsibilities and an essay up to 750 words; no financial record or DACA/TPS document upload required in that guide. Confirm new-cycle materials when published.
eligibility: Published 2026-27 criteria: currently undocumented first-generation immigrants with or without DACA/TPS, arrival before age 16 and November 1,2020, continuous U.S. residence, significant unmet need and no Pell eligibility; high school/GED completion before fall 2026 and 2.5 high school/college GPA. Full-time associate/bachelor’s enrollment at a qualifying partner college. Next-cycle arrival, graduation and GPA rules are not confirmed.
notes: Partner-only; Texas institutions and online/private programs are permitted under specific exceptions, not generally excluded. San Antonio College and South Texas College allow Texas applicants without in-state tuition eligibility. ASU Online is limited to Florida/Texas residents; other online colleges have individual state exclusions. Prior awards cannot be reapplied for; annual renewal needs continuing eligibility and transcript, with June renewal stated on main page. Associate-to-bachelor transfer counts toward the same $33000 total. Complete next-cycle renewal conditions are not published.

provider: Asian & Pacific Islander American Scholarship Fund (APIA Scholars)
name: APIA Scholarship
value: $2,500 one-year awards to $20,000 multi-year awards
deadline: 2027-28 cycle opens November 15, 2026 and closes January 15, 2027 at 5 p.m. ET; notifications April 15, 2027.

The currently linked 2026-27 guide uses one 250-500 wordessay plus personal, academic, financial and activity information, with no initial supporting documents or recommendations. Selected applicants later provide transcript and college/financial confirmation. The 2027-28 guide is not yet published.
eligibility: Currently published criteria still refer to fall 2026: U.S. citizens, nationals or permanent residents, plus citizens of the Marshall Islands, Federated States of Micronesia and Palau, in a degree-seeking U.S. accredited undergraduate program; no prior bachelor’s degree. Full-time and part-time students and all backgrounds were eligible. Confirm 2027-28 rules when updated.
notes: Main page confirms 2027-28 dates but still gives fall 2026 eligibility, and its FAQ/guide remain 2026-27. Prior terms allowed full/part-time associate/first-bachelor’s students of all backgrounds and eligible U.S./national/PR or specifiedPacific citizenship. Need/first-generation status are priorities, not strict requirements. Multi-year award duration and renewal conditions vary and are not public.

name: Earl Woods Scholar Program
value: Renewable annual scholarship for up to four years plus mentorship, internship and summer enrichment help, career development and workshops (dollar amount not stated)
deadline: 2027 application dates not posted on the official page.

eligibility: Graduating high school seniors from a geographic area and/or high school invited to apply, with a minimum 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale, demonstrated financial need and commitment to community service, enrolling full time at a US accredited not-for-profit university.
notes: The specific scholarship eligibility section requires graduating seniors, although the introduction discusses junior/senior support generally. Immediate full-time four-year nonprofit enrollment, demonstrated need, service and mandatory in-person summer Pre-College Retreat/Scholarship Orientation are required. Learning Lab locations do not establish the scholarship invitation list. Amount, full renewal criteria and 2027 dates are not public.

name: ANS Incoming Freshman Scholarship
value: $1,000 each; up to ten awarded annually
deadline: Undated annual schedule: applications November 1; incoming freshmen April 1; notices April 15-May 15; funds after August 20. No explicitly confirmed 2027 cycle or time zone.

General preparation guidance requires institution-submitted transcript and verifies enrollment; confirm the current freshman form because the linked sample is labeled 2025.
eligibility: Graduating high school seniors enrolling full-time in a four-year STEM program with an interest in nuclear science and technology. The specific award page lists high school achievement of more than 3.5 GPA or equivalent; citizenship and GPA weighting are not specified.
notes: Up to ten $1000 incoming-freshman awards annually; repeated awards or continuation rules are not stated. Become an ANS student member after starting undergraduate study before funds are released. AP courses and tests are recommendations, not minimum requirements. Any qualifying STEM discipline may fit; nuclear engineering is not the only major.

name: STEM Stars Actuarial Scholars Program
value: $20,000 total ($5,000 per year for up to four years), plus mentorship, internships, job shadowing and exam resources
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted; applications reopen in the fall. The 2026 deadline was February 27, 2026.
apply: Apply through the official Submittable application manager when the STEM Stars application reopens; it currently redirects to the general manager without an open STEM Stars form.
eligibility: High school seniors who are mathematically talented and interested in the actuarial profession.
notes: Specific page confirms $5000 annually for up to four years, mentorship and summer orientation/free weeklong intensive. Full entry restrictions, academic renewal requirements and current application materials are not public. Actuarial career interest is required; an actuarial-science major is not expressly the only permitted degree.

name: CME Group Beef Industry Scholarship
value: Ten scholarships of $1,500 each
deadline: 2027-28 application and essay due October 9, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. Mountain Time. Obtain both recommendation letters before submission; no separate later recommendation allowance is stated.

eligibility: Graduating high school seniors or full-time undergraduates enrolling at a two- or four-year institution for 2027-2028 who show commitment to a beef-industry career (education, communications, production, research or related). Applicant or family must be a National Cattlemen's Beef Association member.
notes: Ten $1500 awards for the 2027-28 year. Prior winners may apply again; a new application is required rather than automatic renewal. Essay 70%, intent letter 20%, references 10% of scoring. Career goals may include education, communications, production, research or other beef-industry work; no agriculture-only major requirement.

name: ScholarSHPE for Graduating High School Seniors
value: Individual award amounts, duration and renewal vary and are not stated in the accessible current page; the $6 million figure is historical program-wide funding, not an individual award.

Specific offerings allow graduating seniors. SHPE-funded awards do not require citizenship; sponsor awards may add restrictions. Confirm next-cycle and individual award rules.

NSBE Jr. members self-report GPA in MyNSBE and email a verification form signed by their school counselor or NSBE advisor to pci@nsbe.org; allow 2-3 business days for verification.

Duration, renewal terms and full cycle-specific application materials are not published. The older SurveyMonkey page redirects applicants to NSBE’s current site.

name: EAA Post-Secondary Scholarships
value: Individual awards vary with donor funding; amounts are not fixed on the public page. Some named awards are renewable, including Harry E. Arcamuzi for up to three additional years and H.P. Bud Milligan, but full continuation terms are not stated.

eligibility: Award-specific aviation, aerospace and related STEM programs at eligible post-secondary schools. General guidance says age 16+, U.S./Canadian citizenship or residence or valid work/study permission, and no prior master’s or doctoral degree. General post-secondary GPA guidance is 2.5 unweighted, but the Arcamuzi card says 2.0 and other awards require 3.0 or 3.2. Some require prior college coursework, age 19, a pilot certificate, specified location or an EAA Young Eagles connection.
notes: Membership is preferred, not required. The named programs have different academic levels, fields, need preferences and renewal conditions. Public guidance differs on U.S.-only versus U.S./Canada schools and on using funds by March 1 versus within one year of award; confirm the applicable award terms.

Gene Baker and Jim Cook serve AEA member employees or dependents in any major. Other offerings are for member-company employees, convention attendance or private-pilot training.
notes: The current page says the 2026-27 deadline has passed and to check back in October for 2027-28. The Gogo program’s 20-year funding plan is not an individual student’s award duration.

The revised October 2024 PDF required course description/cost, financial-need statement, activities, work history and essays, but its email submission instructions and February 28 deadline differ from the current portal; confirm current materials in the portal.

High school seniors may apply if they meet those training requirements. Additional donor location or school criteria may apply; no trades GPA minimum is stated.

The separate undergraduate award ordinarily excludes seniors but expressly allows seniors already matriculated in college courses with proof. name: NJCPA High School Scholarship
value: $1,500 for one year, plus an NJCPA mentor through college
deadline: Application, essay, counselor form and applicable supporting transcripts/test scores due December 7, 2026 at 11:59 p.m.; time zone unstated. Finalists notified January 4, 2027; required virtual interview January 16, 2027 with no makeup date; results in early March 2027.

eligibility: New Jersey residents attending a New Jersey public, private/parochial or home school as college-bound seniors, U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents, entering a U.S. college next fall. Intend an accounting major or concentration of at least 24 accounting credits. Meet either three-year GPA 3.2 or equivalent, SAT 1260, or ACT 26; the score benchmarks are alternatives to GPA.
notes: A one-year $1500 award paid to the institution after a Scholarship Activation Form, plus mentoring through college. No automatic multi-year scholarship is promised. NJCPA may withdraw or reduce an award at the recipient’s request if it would cause loss of another scholarship. Interview attendance January 16, 2027 is mandatory.
